title: SPECTER
tagline: SPECTER: Stealth Post quantum enabling Cryptographic Transaction Engine for Routing
description:
SPECTER — The private payments layer for onchain money, built to outlive quantum computers.
"Send to a name. Only the recipient can discover, link, or spend it."

═══════════════════════════════════════════
THE PROBLEM
═══════════════════════════════════════════
• Every payment on a public blockchain is a permanent, searchable record — your
  counterparties, balances, salary, and runway are visible to anyone with a block explorer.
• Stealth addresses (Umbra, Fluidkey, ERC-5564) are the current fix: each payment gets a
  fresh, unlinkable address.
• But EVERY one of them is built on ECDH over secp256k1 — the exact math Shor's algorithm
  breaks on a quantum computer.
• This is not theoretical. "Harvest now, decrypt later": adversaries are archiving on-chain
  data today to de-anonymize it tomorrow. Announcement data is public and permanent — it
  cannot be re-encrypted after the fact.
• NIST finalized its post-quantum standards in 2024 (ML-KEM / FIPS 203) and the migration
  is already being mandated. On-chain payment privacy has to be rebuilt once, correctly,
  before that deadline.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
WHAT SPECTER IS
═══════════════════════════════════════════
SPECTER is a production-grade stealth address protocom-vulnerable
key exchange at the heart of stealth addresses with ML-KEM-768 (NIST FIPS 203) — the
standardized post-quantum KEM — while keeping the UX you just pay
to alice.eth or bob.sui.

It ships as a full stack, not a paper:
• specterpq.com — live web wallet: create an identitysend, scan,
  claim, and sweep funds with receipts and claim history.
• @specterpq/sdk — browser-first SDK (Rust → WebAssemys, payment
  construction, and scanning all run in the user's browser.
• specter-api — public-data services: announcement reon, IPFS
  pinning, gas-sponsored relaying.
• specter-* (Rust workspace) — the core: ML-KEM-768 pth
  derivation, batch scanning engine, Turso/libSQL persistence.
• MCP server with per-call x402 payments — AI agents with no API
  key and no subscription.

Live today on Ethereum (mainnet + testnet) and Sui (mainnet + testnet), with ENS and SuiNS
name resolution, plus an announcer contract deployed

HOW IT WORKS — THREE STEPS
═══════════════════════════════════════════
① SET UP (once)
  The recipient's device generates two keypairs — a sa
  post-quantum ML-KEM-768 VIEWING key — bundles the public halves into a meta-address, pins
  it to IPFS, and attaches the CID to an ENS or SuiNSeave the
  device. The meta-address is public and reveals no history.

② SEND (pay to a name)
  The sender resolves alice.eth → meta-address, derivs for this
  payment, sends funds there, and publishes a small announcement to the registry. The sender
  learns nothing about the recipient's other paymentsn can link
  the payment back to alice.eth.

③ RECEIVE (discover and claim)
  The recipient's wallet scans announcements, discardly with a
  1-byte view tag, and recognizes what's theirs. Claiming is one in-app flow: live balances
  for every discovered stealth address, sweep to any ransfer
  signed locally — no private-key export, no wallet import. Produces a downloadable receipt
  (PNG/PDF/JSON) and a per-identity claim history.

how_its_made:
STACK
• Core: Rust workspace, 13 crates, #![forbid(unsafe_code)]. RustCrypto only —
  ml-kem (FIPS 203), sha3 (SHAKE256), k256, blake2, aes-gcm, subtle, zeroize.
• SDK: the same Rust core compiled to WebAssembly, shipped as @specterpq/sdk on npm.
  One codebase is the CLI, the server, and the browser crypto — no reimplementation,
  no chance of the JS and Rust derivations drifting apart.
• API: Axum + tower-http, governor for per-IP rate limits, alloy for Ethereum,
  reqwest for IPFS/RPC. Release profile: LTO, codegen-units=1, panic=abort, strip.
• Web: React 18 + Vite + TypeScript, Tailwind/shadcn, Dynamic Labs (EVM wallets),
  @mysten/dapp-kit + @mysten/suins (Sui), @erc7824/nitrolite (Yellow), TanStack Query.
• Data: Turso (libSQL), pulled in remote-only with default-features=false so release
  builds carry no C library — the container stays tiny and cross-compiles clean.
• Indexing: Envio HyperIndex on Monad testnet, dual-writing to Envio Postgres (GraphQL)
  and Turso (what the scanner reads), plus a standalone viem poller as a fallback path.
• Deploy: Railway (Rust API + poller), Vercel (web), Pinata (IPFS), PostHog.

THE HACKY PARTS WORTH MENTIONING

1) Fitting a 1088-byte ML-KEM ciphertext into ERC-556
ERC-5564's ephemeralPubKey field is bytes32. An ML-KEM-768 ciphertext is 1088 bytes —
it does not fit, and logging it would be brutally exp only
keccak256(ciphertext) as ephemeralKeyHash, while the full ciphertext rides along in the
announce() calldata. The indexer turns on Envio's traor `input`,
decodes the ciphertext back out of the calldata, verifies keccak256(ciphertext) ===
ephemeralKeyHash, and drops the row on mismatch. Cheauctable
off-chain, still ERC-5564-shaped.

2) A metadata blob that is encrypted but still scannable.
Announcement metadata is 77 bytes plaintext: [view_ta32B]
[chain_id 8B][reserved 4B]. Encrypting all of it would break scanning; leaving it clear
publishes the amount. So byte 0 (the view tag) stays ] are
AES-256-GCM sealed → 93 bytes on-chain. Scanners still filter 255/256 events with one
byte comparison and zero crypto; only the recipient rs.
The key and nonce are derived from the ML-KEM shared secret with domain-separated
SHAKE256 — key = SHAKE256("SPECTER_META_ENC_KEY_V1" ‖
nonce = SHAKE256("SPECTER_META_ENC_NONCE_V1" ‖ ss)[..12]. Every encapsulation yields a
fresh shared secret, so nonce reuse is structurally i to be

A view_tag that disagrees with the ciphertext producerectly and

Secrets live only as AES-256-GCM ciphertext in the browser, unlocked by password
